sentences.text: Beibeilong was a bipedal dinosaur with well-developed legs, estimated to reach a length of 7.5 meters and a weight between 1.5 and 2 metric tons.
Its jaws were toothless and equipped with a horny beak known as a rhamphotheca, while its hands featured long fingers ending in large curved claw bones.
Although many oviraptorosaurs possessed feathers, it is suggested that gigantic species like Beibeilong may have had reduced feather coverage due to their large size.

The genus and species Beibeilong sinensis were formally named and described by Pu and colleagues in 2017 based on an embryonic skeleton and partial nest found in Henan Province, China, between 1992 and 1993.
The generic name Beibeilong translates to "baby dragon" in Chinese, while the specific name sinensis refers to China, the country where the species was discovered.
Beibeilong laid large Macroelongatoolithus eggs measuring 40 to 45 cm in length with ruggedly ornamented shells.
Researchers propose that the adult sat in the center of its egg clutch during incubation, likely occupying the central area of the nest devoid of eggs to avoid crushing them.
Beibeilong is classified as a basal member of the family Caenagnathidae, rather than the oviraptorids.
In 2017, researchers considered Beibeilong to be anatomically similar to but more primitive than Gigantoraptor.
Beibeilong lived in China during the Late Cretaceous epoch, approximately 96 to 88 million years ago, specifically within the Cenomanian to Coniacian ages.
It inhabited humid floodplains with rivers in environments ranging from semi-arid to tropical climates where Araucariaceae conifers were largely present.
It is debated whether Beibeilong had teeth; some researchers argue for a dietary shift involving lost teeth, while others reject this based on phylogeny suggesting simple dentaries are ancestral.
It is also debated whether adult oviraptorosaurs found with nests were incubating eggs, laying eggs, or guarding the nest.

Finally, it is probable that the embryo was forcibly removed or taken from one of the underlying eggs, given that the skeleton is not preserved inside an egg and its orientation is inconsistent with the eggs.
